business_scope.primary_industry_name: Automated Global Payroll and Staff Compliance Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain (Unitary National Jurisdiction; no sub-state incorporation tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law - Spanish Commercial Code (Código de Comercio), Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010) and ancillary notarial/registry legislation
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain-Argentina BIT and wider Spain-Latin America investment treaty network
European Union Free Trade Agreements with Mexico, Chile, Japan, and Latin American partners
More than 90 active double taxation avoidance agreements (DTAAs) and the EU tax arbitration convention

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo (AML/CFT Law), as amended by Ley 13/2023; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, which develops the AML law; Real Decreto 1674/2012 and the Registro de Titularidades Reales regulations implementing Directiva (UE) 2015/849 (AMLD4/AMLD5). Ultimate beneficial owner disclosure is codified in Article 4 of Ley 10/2010 and executed registrations are kept at the Banco de España/Colegio de Registradores infrastructure through the Registro de Titularidades Reales.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificado de no denominación (negative name certificate for the S.L.)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC), Ministerio de Justicia
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic issuance; not subject to apostille for official use in Spain

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Escritura de constitución (incorporation deed of Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarial protocol; no apostille required at stage 1

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / certified corporate extract of foreign corporate investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Companies Registry in the foreign jurisdiction of the investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent foreign authority, followed by sworn Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney for the Spanish incorporation representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Spanish Consular Officer or foreign notary in the country of signature
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, depending on treaty status with the country of issue

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: NIE certificate for each non-resident director/shareholder (Número de Identidad de Extranjero)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Comisaría General de Extranjería y Fronteras or Spanish Consulate in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic Spanish administrative issue; foreign validation via Hague Apostille where applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs and beneficial owners against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, Banco de España warnings and domestic PEP databases; automated PEP detection, negative news checks, identity evidence verification, source-of-funds analysis for non-resident ownership, and mandatory suspicious activity reporting to SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales y Faltas Monetarias) under Ley 10/2010.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central - Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social (online service via https://www.registradores.org and RMC terminals of the Ministerio de Justicia)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be expressed in Spanish or in any of the co-official State languages (Catalan, Basque, Galician, Valencian) using Roman alphabet with official accents/diacritics; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated phonetically into Spanish; foreign proper names may be admitted if transliterated and a translation is provided where required; acronyms are limited to those explained in the articles or bylaws; the corporate type suffix 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or 'S.L.' must be included exactly.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bullion or banking-sensitive words requiring public authorization certificates
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the applicant receives the stated reason from the Registro Mercantil Central; the applicant may correct and resubmit a revised name or file a new negative-certificate request after 6 months for re-use of the same proposed name. If the registry or the Directorate General for Legal Security and Public Trust (Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública) has refused registration, the shareholder or representative may file an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) within one calendar month of notification, requesting reconsideration based on trademark rights, novelty, or clarifying that the name does not violate lawful prohibitions; after exhaustion of administrative channels, judicial review may be sought in the National High Court (Audiencia Nacional) within two months.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are permitted as correspondence/administrative facilities, but Spain requires the S.L. to have a physical management address and a registered office where the legal entity is administered; for a cloud-native payroll SaaS platform, a virtual office is acceptable for commercial filings and mail receipt, provided the company maintains documented substance through employees, directors, service contracts, bank accounts, and revenue-generating activity in Spain; SARL notaries and the Commercial Registry will require evidence of the domicile and authorization from the landlord if the address is a shared virtual workplace.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 20% annualized risk of an unannounced physical inspection on the registered office and management premises for a medium-risk enhanced software company in the first three years, with materially higher inspection probability if the registered office is an offshore-style virtual address or shows persistent absence of personnel, physical records, or server/log infrastructure.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registry tariff calculated on capital and registration volume; statutory base, estimated from Spanish registry fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Minimal statutory fee for registry access and notary agency charge; market benchmark for filing assistance

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital; Articles 20 to 23 (formation and registration), Articles 58 and 73 to 74 (minimum capital for Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada), and Articles 209 to 211 (administration and first board resolutions).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (provincial Commercial Registry) for incorporation filing; Registro Mercantil Central for the negative name certificate; Spanish Notary for deed execution.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de constitución (public deed of incorporation) filed with the Registro Mercantil.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SL minimum capital is EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and fully paid in at incorporation. Cash contributions must be deposited in a Spanish bank account opened in the company's name and the bank deposit certificate attached to the deed; no separate escrow account is required by statute.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE COMPANY, HAVING REVIEWED THE INCORPORATION DEED AND THE CERTIFICATE OF CAPITAL DEPOSIT, HEREBY RESOLVES AS FOLLOWS: FIRST, that the subscription and fully paid-up allocation of the share capital, as set out in the deed of incorporation, is approved and confirmed. SECOND, the registered office is fixed at [address], Madrid, Spain, and the management is authorized to execute the lease and public utility contracts. THIRD, the following officers are appointed: [Name] as Chief Executive Officer, [Name] as Company Secretary, and [Name] as Financial Director, each with the powers conferred by the Companies Act and the Bylaws. FOURTH, the officers are jointly and severally authorized to complete the commercial registry filing, tax registration, and banking formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an application for a negative name certificate (certificación negativa de denominación) through the online service or in person at the Central Registry. Submit at least two proposed corporate names in priority order. Pay the applicable tariff and await the certificate confirming no identical or confusingly similar name is already registered.
required_dossiers: NIF/NIE of each founding person or entity
Proposed corporate names in priority order
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is refused due to similarity, resubmit the application with unflagged alternative names. If the registry exceeds the statutory response period, file a written reminder; after 15 further days the applicant may request an express decision and refile if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Bank Account and Deposit Minimum Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish bank or credit institution where the provisional corporate account is opened
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional account in the intended corporate name of the SL in formation and deposit the minimum capital of EUR 3,000. Obtain a bank certificate of deposit (certificado de depósito) addressed to the company. The bank must hold the funds until presentation of the public deed of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Tax identification data of the company in formation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the account due to entity-in-formation status, present the name certificate and draft articles. If the certificate is incomplete, require the bank to issue a fresh certificate stating the amount, currency, depositor and account holder; resubmit to the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Incorporation Deed before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Notary chosen in the jurisdiction of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the notary with all founders and sign the escritura de constitución and the company bylaws. The notary will verify identity, legal capacity, capital deposit and name certificate validity. After signature, the notary issues authorized copies for registration and tax filing.
required_dossiers: Founders' NIE, passports or corporate documents
Anti-money laundering statement required by notarial regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries the deed, correct the identified defects of capacity, capital or statements and re-sign the deed. If Stamp Duty is unpaid, liquidate the corresponding tax before applying for commercial registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pay Transfer Tax and Stamp Duty (AJD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Tributaria de la Comunidad Autónoma where the company is located; AEAT for state-level tax formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 600 in the competent Autonomous Community and pay the Stamp Duty (Modalidad Actos Jurídicos Documentados) applicable to incorporation deeds. Obtain a stamped or computer-validated copy for presentation to the Commercial Registry.
required_dossiers: First notarial copy of the deed
NIE of the taxpayer or legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority challenges the assessment, pay the supplementary tax plus applicable interest. If the company falls under an exemption, obtain the exemption certificate and present it to the registrar to lift any suspension.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company in the Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within two months from execution of the deed, present the first notarial copy and the duplicate to the Commercial Registry. The registrar verifies the legality of the deed and bylaws, inscribes the company and the first board, and returns the registered deed with a certificate of registration.
required_dossiers: Identification and acceptance statements of appointed officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a suspension or refusal, comply with the defects noted in the qualification within the granted period and resubmit. If the company considers the qualification unlawful, appeal to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within 60 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Definitive NIF and Register as Employer
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After commercial registration, apply for the definitive CIF/NIF using Form 036/037 at the AEAT office or online. Register the company with TGSS as an employer and enroll officers, directors and initial employees. Request electronic certificates for tax and Social Security filings.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration from the Commercial Registry
Form 036 or 037 census and tax identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT returns an error in the census data, file a rectification declaration. If TGSS assigns an incorrect CNAE or contribution account, submit a rectification request and, if denied, file an administrative appeal within one month.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ayuntamiento where the registered office is located (Department of Urbanism and Economic Activities), together with the regional Consejería competente en actividad económica and medio ambiente
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de apertura y funcionamiento / Comunicación previa de apertura

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico and the regional Consejería de Medio Ambiente
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 4 (minor activity) for office-based software development and payroll processing services; subject to environmental communication or registration with no full EIA report required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Urban wastewater discharges to municipal sewers must comply with local ordinance limits, generally pH 5.5 to 9.5 and suspended solids below 500 mg/L; VOC emissions are negligible for virtual/cloud operations; electronic and IT equipment waste must be managed under Royal Decree 110/2015 on WEEE; office waste segregation is required under Law 7/2022 on waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Certificado de conformidad de instalaciones contra incendios under Royal Decree 2267/2004, structural load certificate issued by a competent architect for the registered office, and workplace health and safety assessment under Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — the State Tax Administration Agency of Spain; national electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es); some delegated tax competencies exist in the Basque Country and Navarra through their Foral Diputaciones and Hacienda Foral, but the default national authority for the ES_SL entity registered in common-regime Spain is AEAT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL): (i) at incorporation before a notary, the entity obtains a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) through the notary's telematic system; (ii) within 15 days of filing the deed with the Mercantile Registry, submit Form 036/037 (Censo de Obligados Tributarios) to the local AEAT office; (iii) provide certified copy of deed, proof of registration in the Mercantile Registry, identification documents of the legal representative, and evidence of the registered office; (iv) receive the definitive NIF card. For a foreign entity without a permanent establishment making Spanish taxable supplies: apply directly to AEAT for a NIF de entidad no residente (Form 036) and appoint a tax representative resident in Spain (mandatory if the entity invoices Spanish counterparties for services subject to retention, or under AEAT administrative orders), attaching proof of incorporation in home jurisdiction, apostilled articles, and power of attorney.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not offer a US-style check-the-box pass-through election. The SL is automatically subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Corporate Income Tax, Law 27/2014) as a separate legal entity, resident in Spain where it is incorporated or has its registered office/effective place of management. Available statutory elections: (i) tax consolidation regime (Régimen de Consolidación Fiscal, arts. 64-77 LIS) — optional for groups where a parent holds >=90% (>=75% if certain criteria) of a resident subsidiary, elected for 10 years; (ii) Union Temporal de Empresas (UTE) transparency election for joint ventures; (iii) ETVE (Sociedad de Tenencia de Valores Extranjeros) election for holding entities permitting 100% participation exemption on qualifying foreign dividends and capital gains; (iv) partial/revaluation reserve opt-in under Ley 16/2012; (v) R&D and Intellectual Property (Patent Box) regime election — 60% partial exemption of qualifying IP income under art. 23 LIS and the transitory grandfathering; (vi) ATAD hybrid mismatch rules are mandatory adjustment provisions, not elective.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.territorial_scope_notes: Resident entities are taxed on worldwide income; subject to ordinary 25% CIT rate (27% for credits; 25% standard; 15% for newly created entities qualifying for reduced rate on first 2 profitable years, capped basis), with 19% for NIF non-resident entities on Spanish-source income unless exempt and 24% branch profit remittance tax (composition).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.vat_office_registration_path: IVA registration is integrated with Form 036/037 under AEAT; the same taxpayer census file covers both Corporate Income Tax and VAT obligations. For the SL, registration with IVA before commencing commercial activity is mandatory with no generally applicable turnover threshold.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido) — Spanish national VAT implemented under Ley 37/1992 and Royal Decree 1624/1992 in line with Council Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for Spanish-established taxable persons: any entity carrying out economic activities performed in Spanish territory must be registered for IVA before starting operations (arts. 3 and 164 LIVA). For intra-EU distance sales of goods to Spanish consumers by EU non-established suppliers, the annual pan-EU remote-sales threshold is EUR 10,000 of aggregated supplies, above which the supplier must register in Spain or use the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) scheme; for B2C digital services and telecommunications/broadcasting, OSS registration is used. For non-EU suppliers, VAT registration in Spain is due as soon as any taxable supply is made to a Spanish recipient unless the reverse charge applies (for B2B) or OSS IOSS is used for distance sales. The simplified SME regime (Régimen Simplificado) applies to business persons with turnover <= EUR 250,000 per total supplies and <= EUR 150,000 for agricultural/forestry/fishing acquisitions, but this is a calculation regime, not an exemption threshold: registration in the IVA census remains substantive.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain has a legislated e-invoicing regime and fiscal integrity mandate. (1) SII — Suministro Inmediato de Información: mandatory for taxable persons with business volume > euro 6,000,000, VAT groups, and certain sectors; requires sending VAT book records (records of issued/received invoices, capital goods, intra-EU chain transactions) to AEAT within 4 calendar days (8 days in certain cases) using XML/EDI web services through the AEAT electronic headquarters with a recognized digital certificate; this is post-issuance transmission, not a clearance/authorisation model. (2) VeriFactu (Ley 18/2022 'Crea y Crece', developed by RD 1007/2023): all businesses, including SII-exempt SMEs, must ensure their invoicing software meets integrity, traceability, and authenticity requirements (hash 'vuelco' generation, QR digital fingerprint with VeriFactu XML) and provide an immediate electronic report to AEAT upon request; the Mandatory Issuance of Facturae-standard e-invoices for B2B transactions applies progressively from 2025 for issuers with revenue > euro 8,000,000 and from 2026 for smaller businesses under the Royal Decree implementing Ley Crea y Crece. (3) Large digital/SaaS exporters: no special prior fiscal clearance is applied to electronic issue, but ZK-drive invoices may be accepted; AEAT requires that all invoices contain the required fields (art. 6 RD 1619/2012) and be electronically archived for 6 years, with full integrity and traceability compliant with VeriFactu.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% IVA applies to true exports (envíos/transportes de bienes) physically leaving the European Union, per art. 21 LIVA: (i) dispatch or transport of tangible goods to a non-EU destination performed or declared by the exporter, evidenced by the Customs export declaration (DUA/DEX); (ii) ancillary services, freight, and services related to exported goods (customs, loading, warehousing, processing) under art. 22 LIVA; (iii) international transport services of goods to non-EU points, and services directly linked to goods in transit (art. 21.3 LIVA). For the ES_SL Payroll-SaaS ISIC 6201 scope: (i) B2B services (license/SaaS) delivered to a recipient genuinely established outside the EU are 'not subject' to Spanish IVA under the place-of-supply rule (art. 69.1 LIVA) — not formally an export but a zero-rated/out-of-scope supply: invoice must identify the Spanish supplier and foreign recipient, with no IVA, and entry in the Export/International Services registry; (ii) B2C supply of digital payroll/HR software to non-EU consumers is outside Spanish VAT as the place of supply follows the consumer's jurisdiction; (iii) services to EU B2B customers (reverse charge/ intra-EU) are zero-rated where the recipient provides a valid VIES number and invoice states 'IVA no devengado — inversion del sujeto pasivo / art. 84.1.2 LIVA'; raw data/export stipulations require the customer's country to be evidenced by residency certificates (Certificate of Residence / VIES validation) for refund claims of input IVA on export-related costs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading (B/L), Air Waybill (AWB) or CMR international consignment note
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank credit advice evidencing EUR/foreign currency proceeds (Justificante de Cobro del Extranjero)
Commercial invoice with explicit 0% VAT and legal basis citation (art. 21 LIVA)
Packing list and INCOTERMS-determined export contract
Certificate of non-EU destination ISO country code and consignee tax ID / Certificate of Residence (for services)
Customs release/clearance proof and, for intra-EU movements, Intrastat filings or VIES validation record
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT strictly audits export zero-rating and out-of-scope treatment under the 4-year limitation window (extended to 5 years where fraudulent misdeclaration is proven). Non-compliant zero-rating constitutes an infrastructure offence of partial/incomplete tax base (infracción leve/grave): penalties range from 15% to 50% of the evaded tax where the debtor corrects voluntarily with delay, up to 50%–150% of the VAT clawed back where inaccurate/hidden data are involved, and up to 100%–150% if wholly false documents or forged invoices were used; the 'recargo de apremio' of 26% applies after enforcement without prior notice; interest at the statutory default rate (currently 3.75% but recommitted annually) runs from the due date of the return. Retrospective clawback invalidates input VAT deductions on export-related costs and the supplier's output zero-rating is replaced by application of the standard 21% rate, with recalculation of the VAT payable and corresponding refund order. For wholly artificial arrangements (sham exports) or deliberate fraud, AEAT files criminal referrals for fraud under art. 305 of the Spanish Criminal Code (fraud > EUR 120,000 triggers criminal liability, with imprisonment 1–5 years and fines of 2–6 times the defrauded amount); the corporate entity itself may also be prosecuted under art. 310 bis / 310 for accounting falsification. The 'inward remittance' deadline of 180 days for bringing hard-currency proceeds into the bank account is an administrative/bank-realised rule for matching proof of consideration, but for correct EUR proceeds no separate FX deadline applies; nonetheless, AEAT will treat unrepatriated invoiced proceeds more than 180 days after dispatch as an indication that the supply was not genuinely exported, triggering the clawback, penalty and interest analysis above.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), supervised by the European Central Bank (ECB)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain maintains a fully convertible Euro regime for both current and capital accounts. Capital account transactions, including profit remittances and equity investments, face no restrictions. Profit remittances to foreign shareholders are permitted without prior approval, subject to standard corporate and tax filings.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds is required under Spanish or EU law. Exporters may freely retain and utilize export receipts. There are no statutory timelines or mandatory conversion ratios.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasible via licensed EMI providers such as Wise or Revolut Business for cross-border payments and payroll disbursements. Legal constraints include adherence to Spanish AML/CFT regulations, potential registration as an EMI under EU Payment Services Directive (PSD2), and compliance with MiCA for crypto-related elements if applicable.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for initial corporate KYC onboarding and director interviews at Spanish commercial banks. Remote account opening is generally not permitted for new entities without established banking relationships or specific regulatory exemptions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media or sanctions screening alerts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive source of funds and source of wealth documentation, beneficial ownership register, and independent legal opinions confirming legitimacy of transactions

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction exposure or PEP status
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence package including transaction narratives, third-party verification reports, and proof of economic purpose aligned with payroll SaaS operations

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing via SWIFT MT103 or SEPA Instant to Spanish IBAN accounts. Required purpose codes include 'CAP' for capital contributions and 'INV' for investments. Verification mandates supporting documentation such as company incorporation deed, shareholder agreements, and valuation reports for non-cash contributions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails utilize SWIFT MT103 for international wire transfers. Trade settlements may employ Commercial Letters of Credit (LCs) under UCP 600 rules. SEPA transfers apply for intra-EU disbursements, while global payroll or vendor payments follow standard correspondent banking protocols.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (Cuentas Anuales) approved by shareholders and deposited at the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil of the registered office (Provincial Mercantile Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar year-end: shareholders’ meeting to approve accounts by 30 June; deposit within one month of approval (no later than 31 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Mercantile Registry closes the company’s file (cierre registral), preventing registration of share transfers and appointments; directors may be fined EUR 1,200–EUR 6,000 under Ley de Sociedades de Capital.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Modelo 200 / Impuesto sobre Sociedades)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days from the sixth month after the tax year-end; for calendar year-end no later than 25 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge from 5% to 20% of the assessed amount plus late-payment interest; if submitted after official requirement, penalty may reach 150% of unpaid tax; administrative strike-off does not apply to tax returns.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 and 30 January of the year following the taxable period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Spontaneous late filing surcharge (5%–20%) plus interest; flat penalties for late or inaccurate informative VAT schedules; omission penalties can range from EUR 50 to EUR 200.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Informative Statement of Third-Party Transactions (Modelo 347) — required if aggregate transactions with any third party exceed EUR 3,005.06
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 and 28 February (29 February in leap years) following the reporting calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Undisclosed or incorrect data may be penalised with a fixed charge per entry and minimum EUR 100–EUR 1,000 depending on volume; late filing also subject to interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO annual confirmation and update of ultimate beneficial owner data (Registro de Titulares Reales) via the Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil / Registro de Titulares Reales (Ministry of Justice)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually aligned with the annual accounts deposit (no later than 31 July for calendar year-end); within one month of any share transfer altering beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-updated beneficial-ownership data constitutes an AML offence under Law 10/2010, with administrative fines and potential restriction on registration; repeated breaches may trigger judicial strike-off procedures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SL must be audited when, at year-end, it meets at least two of the three small-company thresholds for two consecutive years: total assets > EUR 4,000,000; net turnover > EUR 8,000,000; average workforce > 50. An audit is also mandatory if shareholders holding at least 5% of capital so request.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP — Plan General Contable (RD 1514/2007, updates; PGC PyME for SMEs). IFRS-EU applies only to consolidated accounts of groups, not mandatory for a standalone non-listed SL.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain does not require a separate annual UBO return. The SL must keep the Register of Members current, notify the Mercantile Registry of any transfer of shares or change of control within one month, and restate beneficial-ownership data as part of the annual accounts deposit and director certification.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de la Junta/Administradores)
Register of Contracts with Sole Shareholder (Libro Registro de Contratos con el Socio Único) — only while single-member

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general rate for Spanish-resident SL companies. Qualifying newly created entities generally apply 15% in the first tax period with a positive taxable base and the immediately following tax period, subject to statutory exclusions. Other reduced rates may apply according to company size and tax period; verify the rate for the relevant year.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Potential incentives include the 15% start-up rate, the Patent Box regime for qualifying income from certain intangible assets, and research and development and technological innovation tax credits. Eligibility, limits, documentation, and recapture rules apply. No general tax holiday applies.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite. Net operating tax losses generally carry forward without a time limit, subject to annual utilization limits, anti-trafficking rules, and a general minimum offset of EUR 1 million; the applicable percentage limitation depends on turnover and tax period.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Corporate Income Tax return, filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT) electronic headquarters using an authorized electronic certificate. Modelo 202 is used for advance corporate tax payments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Modelo 200: Annual. Modelo 202: Three advance-payment periods annually, where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Modelo 200: Within 25 calendar days following the six months after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the usual filing window is 1–25 July. Modelo 202: Generally due during the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December; payment may be required even when the annual return is not yet filed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company tax identification number (NIF), legal name, tax domicile, tax period, and applicable return type.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned Spanish SL files as a Spanish-resident taxpayer and uses its Spanish NIF. Report foreign ownership accurately; non-resident shareholders do not make the SL a non-resident company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the accounting profit or loss and reconcile it to the taxable base through statutory tax adjustments, including nondeductible expenses, exempt income, depreciation differences, and related-party adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Spanish tax rules to the SL's worldwide taxable income, subject to applicable treaty relief and foreign tax credit rules. Maintain supporting records for cross-border transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the taxable base after permitted adjustments and apply available loss carryforwards subject to statutory limits and anti-abuse rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document the origin, amount, and availability of losses. A change in ownership may restrict use where statutory conditions are met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax rate, credits, and tax due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the rate applicable to the company and tax period; claim eligible deductions and credits with required supporting documentation; calculate net corporate tax due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim incentives only if the SL meets Spanish statutory conditions. Foreign tax credits require evidence of foreign tax paid and are limited under Spanish law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Withholdings, advance payments, and final balance
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit Spanish withholdings and Modelo 202 payments and report the resulting amount payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile payments to AEAT records and retain certificates for withholding taxes and advance payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complete applicable disclosures for related-party transactions, tax incentives, tax losses, and other required schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose cross-border related-party transactions and maintain transfer-pricing support. Separate reporting obligations, including Modelo 232 where applicable, may apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without a prior AEAT requirement generally attracts a fixed percentage surcharge based on delay, increasing by one percentage point for each full month of delay during the first 12 months; after 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15% plus late-payment interest. A return filed after an AEAT requirement may incur a tax-infringement penalty, generally 50%–150% of the unpaid amount, depending on severity and aggravating factors. Late payment, inaccurate returns, and failure to make advance payments may attract separate interest and penalties. Electronic filing failures should be corrected promptly; statutory penalty treatment depends on the breach and circumstances.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, Corporate Income Tax advance-payment form, filed and paid electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly payment periods in April, October, and December; not a quarterly corporate income tax return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally, the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December. The amount is calculated using the statutory method applicable to the taxpayer, including the prior-year tax-liability method or, where required or elected, the current-year taxable-base method.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the company's NIF, legal name, tax period, and advance-payment period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish SL's NIF and its own tax-period information, regardless of the residence of its shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify the applicable calculation method and enter the statutory base figures and prior payments required for that method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the method required by Spanish law based on the company's circumstances and prior return data; retain the calculation and supporting records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the amount due, apply permitted credits, and provide the payment or direct-debit details required by the electronic filing system.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure payment is made from an accepted account or through an authorized payment channel and reconcile it to the annual Modelo 200.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to make or pay an advance payment may result in late-payment interest and tax penalties under the General Tax Law. Penalty exposure depends on whether the omission is corrected voluntarily or follows an AEAT requirement, the unpaid amount, and the conduct involved.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% generally applies to dividends paid by a Spanish company to non-residents, subject to exemptions and treaty relief. A qualifying EU parent may obtain an exemption under the Spanish implementation of the Parent-Subsidiary Directive, generally requiring a qualifying direct holding of at least 5% for an uninterrupted one-year period and satisfaction of beneficial ownership and anti-abuse conditions. Other domestic exemptions may apply in specified cases.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, provide the Spanish payer with a valid certificate of tax residence issued by the competent authority in the recipient's residence jurisdiction, generally covering the relevant period, and any declarations or evidence required to establish beneficial ownership, treaty entitlement, participation, and absence of abuse. The payer generally applies relief at source only where documentation supports it. If tax is withheld at the domestic rate, the recipient may seek a refund from AEAT using the applicable non-resident tax refund procedure and supporting residence and payment evidence. Treaty rates and conditions vary by treaty and income classification.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic non-resident withholding rate is generally 19% for Spanish-source interest and royalties, subject to statutory exemptions, including qualifying EU-related-party interest or royalty exemptions where all conditions are met. Applicable income tax treaties may reduce the rate, often subject to beneficial ownership and other treaty requirements. Confirm the relevant treaty, characterization, source, recipient status, and documentation before payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Spanish related-party transactions must generally be valued at arm's length. Documentation exemptions and thresholds are transaction- and taxpayer-specific: documentation is generally not required for transactions with the same related party that do not exceed EUR 250,000 at market value during the tax period, subject to exclusions. Simplified documentation may be available to entities or groups with net turnover below EUR 45 million, subject to exceptions. Spanish rules require a group master file in specified cases, including where group net turnover reaches EUR 45 million; Country-by-Country reporting generally applies to qualifying groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million. Confirm current statutory rules and exceptions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not apply a separate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. Spanish transfer-pricing rules, beneficial-ownership requirements, controlled foreign company rules, general anti-abuse provisions, and business-purpose and substance analysis can challenge arrangements lacking genuine functions, assets, risks, decision-making, or commercial rationale. Treaty and EU directive benefits may be denied under applicable anti-abuse rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing taxable income, fabricating expenses or invoices, maintaining undeclared accounts, or intentionally filing materially false returns to avoid Spanish tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax penalties are generally 50%–150% of the unpaid tax depending on the infringement and aggravating factors, in addition to tax, interest, and surcharges. Tax fraud may be criminal where the amount defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000 per tax and period: imprisonment is generally one to five years and a fine of one to six times the defrauded amount. Aggravated cases may carry imprisonment of two to six years and a fine of two to six times the amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face criminal liability where they participate in or knowingly facilitate the offense. Under the General Tax Law, directors may also incur subsidiary or joint and several liability in specified circumstances, including deliberate cooperation in tax violations or failure to perform required duties. Personal liability is not automatic; statutory conditions and due process apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing related-party services, software, intellectual property, financing, or cost allocations other than at arm's length; failing to maintain required records; or omitting required related-party disclosures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may adjust taxable income, assess additional tax and interest, and impose penalties under the General Tax Law. Specific documentation and reporting penalties may apply, subject to statutory caps and the facts of the case.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable where statutory requirements for participation, cooperation, or subsidiary liability are satisfied. A pricing adjustment alone does not automatically pierce the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, or royalties without withholding or remitting required tax, or applying treaty relief without valid residence and entitlement evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer may be assessed for the unpaid withholding tax, late-payment interest, and applicable penalties. Relief may be denied where beneficial ownership, treaty eligibility, or anti-abuse requirements are not met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face statutory tax liability or criminal exposure where they knowingly direct or facilitate unlawful withholding failures; liability depends on their conduct and the applicable statutory tests.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False invoicing, bookkeeping, or electronic record manipulation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using fictitious suppliers, suppressing payroll or SaaS revenue, altering accounting records, or creating false evidence to reduce taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessments, interest, administrative penalties, and, where the criminal tax-fraud threshold and intent are met, criminal prosecution may apply. Forgery or accounting offenses may trigger additional liability under the Criminal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and other individuals who authorize, implement, or knowingly benefit from falsification may incur personal administrative or criminal liability. Corporate form does not protect an individual from liability for personal wrongdoing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money laundering and suspicious payment flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using payroll or payment infrastructure to disguise criminal proceeds, process transactions without required customer due diligence, or fail to report suspicious activity where the company is a subject obliged under applicable AML rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Where the SL is subject to Spanish AML obligations, breaches may result in administrative sanctions under Law 10/2010, including significant fines, public reprimands, and restrictions on management or activity. Money laundering may also constitute a criminal offense, with penalties dependent on the offense and circumstances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers, compliance officers, and other responsible individuals may incur administrative or criminal liability for personal participation or culpable failures where statutory requirements are met. AML subject status depends on the company's actual activities; payroll software alone does not automatically establish it.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive shell structure or artificial treaty arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing income through a nominal company without genuine functions or commercial purpose to obtain treaty, EU, or tax-rate benefits, or misrepresenting the beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may deny exemptions or treaty benefits, recharacterize transactions, assess tax and interest, and impose penalties for inaccurate reporting or evasion. Criminal consequences require satisfaction of the relevant criminal-law elements and thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for their own participation in fraud or for statutory tax debts where applicable conditions are met. Travel restrictions or imprisonment are not automatic consequences of a tax assessment and require separate legal grounds and procedures.
